cues: A thick protective skin surrounds sweet, juicy flesh in many warm-climate fruits sold fresh.
As they ripen, tropical fruits develop fragrant sweetness beneath colorful coverings that shield their soft interiors.
A cross-section shows tender edible flesh enclosed by a distinct outer layer.
Sweet, fibrous flesh gives some tropical produce a pleasantly substantial texture when eaten fresh.
Warm growing regions yield fleshy fruits with skins that change appearance as their interiors ripen.
Produce displays often group bright-colored, peel-covered fruits with soft centers among tropical specialties.
After its protective covering is removed, ripe fruit can be cut into small pieces for a fresh snack.
Yellow flesh, a sweet scent, and a removable skin are familiar traits of tropical fruit.
